page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the AMD EPYC processor platform. The instance delivers 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs using simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. Compute resources are provisioned on dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 7J13 silicon, ensuring predictable core allocation for sustained processing demands.

Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance configuration does not include local disk storage, requiring external network-attached block volumes for persistent disk storage and file systems. The instance includes no discrete GPU hardware acceleration, focusing strictly on general CPU compute execution. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Because of its balanced core-to-memory ratio, this flexible instance type suits workloads such as application hosting, enterprise web serving, backend application servers, integration pipelines, and continuous integration environments. Without bundled local solid-state drives, deployments requiring high-throughput disk input/output rely on attached block storage capabilities.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7J13 processor. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz with 2 threads per core. The server is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators, meaning persistent data storage must be backed by remote block volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for external network access. With dedicated compute resources and proportional memory provisioning, VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-64 is well configured for general-purpose workloads, including multi-tier web applications, backend application services, microservices hosting, and build or integration pipelines.
